## Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby

A reflow oven in standby still draws **36% of its 70 kW rating — about 25.2 kW per oven** for as long as it is left running, which is a large idle load that produces nothing. A properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend. The correct procedure is to leave ovens on for 30 minutes after the line stops (for heat-up), then switch them fully off — and only when no boards are inside — rather than leaving them in standby over the weekend or holidays. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

## Excess energy in incident S5

In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), RF-02 was left in standby all weekend. The weekend energy was about **1,556 kWh** versus about **346 kWh** normal, an excess of about **1,210 kWh** from that single oven. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

Note that the off-schedule rule only flags this after 120 minutes above 20% of rating, so the real benefit comes from switching the oven off proactively rather than detecting it afterward. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

answer:
Based on the demand management procedure:

**Shed first:** EV charging (EV-01) is the first action in the load-shed playbook — it's paused at 100% because it has no effect on production. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]

**Never shed:** The following loads must never be shed:
- Server room (DC-01)
- Running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04)
- Reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03)

[source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]

For reference, the full shed order (least disruptive first) is: (1) pause EV charging, (2) delay the next burn-in loading (BI-01, BI-02), (3) raise chilled-water setpoint +1°C (CH-01, CH-02), (4) lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar (AC-01, AC-02, AC-03). [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]
